payload.claim: [host-filed criterion probe] tests/test_spec_review.py::test_a_draft_with_faults_goes_back_to_the_same_session_naming_each_line stayed green with the criterion's own edit applied to saffron/spec_review.py. The claim was "`run_spec_writer` takes a required `faults` callable, returning a `DraftFaults`, and a required `emit`. Once a turn's `spec` field validates, it calls `faults` on that text. A text with no fault lines ends the session as today. A text with fault lines goes back to the same session as a send-back of two turns. The first is a work turn. It resumes the session's latest id with tools and no `output_format`, and its budget is `SPEC_WRITER_SEND_BACK_BUDGET_USD`. Its prompt is `SPEC_WRITER_SEND_BACK_PROMPT` then every fault line, one per line. The second is the existing extraction turn, with `SPEC_WRITER_EXTRACT_PROMPT` and its options unchanged, resumed at the work turn's id. Each turn's `last_cost_usd` is the turn before it capped at its own budget. Every turn's cost and turns join the session's. `faults` also reads the text a send-back returns. The session's text is then the newest text that parsed, or the newest text of all when none parsed. At most `SPEC_WRITER_SEND_BACKS` send-backs run, read at call time, and the default is 1. `SPEC_WRITER_SESSION_USD` is the first turn and one extraction turn, plus each send-back's work and extraction budgets, $23.00 today. The witness drives a text the first extraction returns and one the re-ask returns, a text with no faults, faults that persist, a returned text that does not parse with and without an earlier one that did, two send-backs with the bound patched to 2, and last costs both under and over each cap.". Under the edit the whole `tests` gate failed tests/test_follow_up.py::test_a_hundred_dollar_night_writes_one_follow_up_at_the_writer_ceiling, tests/test_spec_review.py::test_a_spec_writer_session_returns_the_extraction_turns_spec, and the criterion's witness did not fail.
